title: Caesar Salad a la Paul Corbin
tagline: The card admits it's a little vague. Anchovies, a coddled egg, no bottle.
description: A family-card Caesar: a whole can of anchovies and garlic mashed by hand, olive and corn oil, lemon juice and a coddled egg, tossed with romaine, Parmesan and croutons.
ingredients: 2 bunches romaine lettuce, washed and dried
steps: Coddle the egg: lower it, in the shell, into boiling water for 1 minute, then run it under cold water.
In the salad bowl, mash the anchovies and garlic to a fine texture.
Add both oils and the lemon juice and stir with a wooden spoon. Crack in the coddled egg and stir until creamy.
Add the romaine and sprinkle with Parmesan.
Mix gently and add the croutons.
notes: The card lists olive oil and Mazola oil but only mentions olive oil in the steps. Both go in.
The card doesn't say how to coddle. One minute in boiling water is the standard method: the white just starts to set, the yolk stays raw.
A coddled egg is mostly raw. For kids, pregnancy, older people or anyone with a weak immune system, use a pasteurized egg.
The romaine has to be completely dry or the dressing slides off.
A whole can of anchovies is a lot. That's the point of this one.
troubleshooting: Thin, watery dressing → wet lettuce; spin or towel it dry.
Gritty anchovy bits → not mashed enough; mash to a paste before the oil goes in.
Soggy croutons → added too early; they go on last, right before serving.
source: Adapted from a family recipe card (a la Paul Corbin)
